reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism involves dual-eye innervation where paralysis disrupts coordinated movement. When the right eye is paralyzed, it halts mid-movement while the left eye completes its rotation. This creates a spatial mismatch in visual field alignment. The brain interprets this through afferent signals from the healthy eye, which override proprioceptive feedback from the paralyzed eye. The resulting perceptual conflict manifests as optical vertigo—where the image remains static on the retina yet is perceived as moving. This duality is mathematically modeled as a vector difference in angular displacements (Δθ), with a net motion signal (F_net) dominated by afferent inputs. The breakdown occurs when F_a > F_c, causing a misalignment in perceived vs actual motion. The system's failure mode is thus a conflict between sensory input and motor output, resolved through Bayesian inference in GSI and state transition in GSE.
